definitions.EASY: One semantic cue with little plausible category competition.
definitions.MODERATE: One meaningful competing category; the candidate and bounded context resolve it.
definitions.HARD: Multiple plausible cues; resolution requires a semantic distinction rather than category keywords.
definitions.ADVERSARIAL: Realistic surface wording favors a specific plausible wrong class; context or a rubric distinction supports another defensible label. Not nonsense, prompt injection, or ambiguity alone.

rules: Assign difficulty before blind review and record the competing interpretation privately.
Do not change difficulty because reviewers agree or disagree.
Ambiguous, disputed, unresolved mixed or rubric-sensitive examples belong in TAXONOMY_STRESS, never primary accuracy.
Do not expose difficulty, cohort, family, author rationale or boundary tags to the provider or blind reviewer.
Context supplies natural evidence or conversation, not an explanation of the correct category.
Adversarial cases must name a plausible surface lure privately; negation alone is not evidence of difficulty.
